name: Auxiliares Insidiatorum (limitan)

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

abilities.name: War Cry
abilities.text: Reduces the morale of nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Light Shield Wall
abilities.text: The unit moves into a close formation and raises shields.

attributes.name: Stalk
attributes.text: This unit can move hidden in any terrain.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Guerrilla Deployment
attributes.text: This unit can deploy outside of the deployment zone.

attributes.name: Hide (grass)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in long grass until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Ignore Terrain
attributes.text: Speed penalties caused by the terrain are ignored by this unit.

short: The name Insidiatorum, literally can be translated as «ambushers». Auxilia (latin) - an auxiliary unit of the Roman army. There is a strong opinion that auxilia units consisted of barbarians-volunteers, the conditions of service of which were determined by a special agreement. For instance, Vegetius directly mentions that the legions were composed of Roman citizens, and the auxilia of barbarians. Vegetius divides the barbarians themselves into «allies» and «Foederati». If under the second we can understand the representatives of tribes with whom a special pact (foedus) was concluded, the first, apparently, should include the tribes, originally or for quite a long time living on the territory of the Empire. About the internal organisation of the auxilia nothing is definitely known, but most likely, the structure of these units in the 4th century was no different from the legions. While the legions were composed of forcefully conscripted Romanised barbarians who lived on the territory of the Empire, in the auxilia served mainly volunteers from the Germanic tribes beyond the Rhine. Such system led to the fact that the auxiliaries became superior to the legionnaires in terms of their combat qualities. In the 4th century it was a recognised fact that the more barbaric was the detachment, the higher was its combat value; the process of steady enhancement of auxiliary troops, which lasted for centuries, came to an end in this era - auxilia came to be considered more capable and reliable than legions.
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
